brief: BofA systematic flows monitor, data as of 11-Sep-26. Several faster CTA trend signals rolled over on this week's equity declines, so the most risk-averse models stopped out of Euro Stoxx 50 longs on Wednesday and Russell 2000 longs on Thursday, while medium- and long-term signals stayed constructive and overall equity positioning stayed net long. By Friday morning the S&P 500 traded within roughly 50bps of key stop-out levels, but a sharp risk-on reversal helped by lower oil prices pushed markets away from triggers and prevented broader systematic selling. Positioning is therefore less robust than a week ago and the near-term flow outlook is biased toward more selling if equities weaken, with the model estimating $157bn of systematic selling in a down market against $15bn of buying in an up market. Trend followers held elevated US Treasury and Bund shorts as global yields rose, bought JPY through a second week of yen appreciation, and added crude longs to their most bullish level since 4-Mar after oil gained more than 9% for a second straight week on Iran hostilities. SPX hedger gamma fell to $2.9bn and hedgers are net short $0.7bn across next week's expiries into the FOMC.
